title: Speculative decode runtime: model routing, acceptance metrics, and graceful fallback
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We want to add speculative decoding support in the serving runtime to reduce tail latency and improve throughput by running low-cost model variants in parallel with higher-quality models. This ticket defines runtime hooks for: (1) model routing decisions for speculative candidates, (2) acceptance metrics to decide when to commit speculative outputs, and (3) a graceful fallback path when speculation fails or is inconsistent. The feature needs to interoperate with kernel selection, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling.
non_goals: This ticket does not cover model training or automatic candidate generation. It also does not implement new quantization kernels; it reuses existing kernel selection infrastructure.
goals: 1) Define a routing policy abstraction that can express candidate sets (primary, speculative candidates, compatibility rules). 2) Implement an acceptance metric set (agreement, confidence delta, latency delta) and an evaluation loop. 3) Add scheduler-level support to launch speculative workers during prefill/early decode and cancel if primary completes earlier. 4) Provide observability (per-request traces, acceptance rate, wasted-work ratio) and a safe rollout plan with feature flag and canary config.
design_summary: High level: introduce a "speculative_router" component in the runtime control plane. The router exposes an API: chooseCandidates(request_context) -> ordered candidate list. Each candidate includes model_variant, kernel_profile_hint, and max_decode_token_budget. The decode scheduler will use the candidate list to spawn speculative workers at configurable pipeline stages: immediately after prefill, at N tokens into decode, or on latency threshold. Acceptance is determined by a pluggable comparator module: compareOutputs(primary, candidate) -> accept|reject with reasons. Native acceptance rules: token-level top-K agreement (default top-1), logit-margin threshold, and latency-priority override for low-latency tiers. Fallback: if candidate accepted, commit candidate output and cancel primary; if rejected or timeout, keep primary output. Metrics: acceptance_rate, latency_improvement_p90, wasted_token_work_ratio.
implementation_steps: 1) SpecRouter API + config schema (YAML) and default policy; add tests. 2) Wire router into request handling path; ensure kernel selection hints pass to kernel_selector module. 3) Extend scheduler to support paired speculative worker lifecycle and prefill-aware KV-cache sharing. 4) Implement comparator primitives (topk_agreement, logit_margin, consensus_hash) and a pluggable interface. 5) Add tracing hooks and telemetry events (spec_start, spec_accept, spec_reject, spec_cancel). 6) Create canary rollout with per-customer and per-model opt-in flags. 7) Document operator controls in Console for tuning candidate sets and token budgets.
acceptance_criteria:
- API: chooseCandidates can return candidate lists in under 200 microseconds in 95% of calls.
- Functional: end-to-end speculative workflow passes integration tests that validate accept/reject flows and KV-cache consistency.
- Metrics: when enabled on synthetic latency-heavy workload, p95 tail latency reduces by >=15% with wasted_token_work_ratio < 30%.
- Observability: Console surface shows acceptance_rate, latency_improvement_p50/p95, wasted_token_work_ratio, and top failure reasons.
- Safety: ability to disable speculation per-tenant with immediate effect and no request loss.
- Security: security review completed and KMS/HSM interactions unaffected.
telemetry_and_metrics: Events: spec_request_start, spec_candidate_launched, spec_candidate_ready, spec_accept, spec_reject, spec_cancel, spec_error.\nMetrics: spec_acceptance_rate (per-model, per-tenant), spec_latency_win_rate (per-model), wasted_token_work_ratio, avg_spec_overhead_ms, spec_fallback_count.\nDashboards: runtime-1.22/speculative-overview and per-model breakdown. Suggested queries in ClickHouse and Grafana will be added in follow-ups.
rollback_and_fallback: Runtime feature flagging with immediate disable. Canary plan: start with 5% traffic for internal customers -> 20% partner tenants -> broader rollout. If wasted_token_work_ratio exceeds threshold (default 45%) or spec_error rate > 1% for 10m, auto-disable for the tenant and alert SRE. Must ensure KV cache consistency: speculative workers attach read-only to the shared KV snapshot; only primary writes commit. If speculative candidate needs state mutation (should be rare), run in isolated mode and treat as expensive path.
tests:
- unit tests for SpecRouter logic and comparator primitives.
- integration tests with kernel_selector mocking to verify hint propagation.
- load test scenarios: synthetic long-decoder sequences and short chat bursts.
- A/B experiment harness to measure p50/p95 latency and user-visible quality delta (using eval prompt sets).
- Fuzz tests for acceptance comparator edge cases.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: wasted GPU cycles increase cost unexpectedly. Mitigation: strict token_budget defaults, per-tenant limits, telemetry alerts and auto-disable policy.\nRisk: inconsistency between decoded outputs caused by KV-cache divergence. Mitigation: share KV snapshot and only commit writes from primary; require compatibility check.\nRisk: acceptance metric may prefer wrong outputs, degrading quality. Mitigation: conservative default rules (require topk agreement or logit_margin >= 2.0), run offline evals to tune thresholds, and provide per-model overrides.
